descriptions.text: Zero pity. The notorious MEV bot known as 0xbad has fallen on hard times, just like the rest of us. After 75 days of exploiting value from unexpecting users, this mempool menace backfired on its owner, creating a beautiful display of on-chain karma.

Arbitrary call via callFunction. Vulnerable code snippet: In this case dYdX called "callFunction" on 0xbad. Unfortunately for 0xbad, their code allowed for arbitrary execution. Need to decompiled: https://etherscan.io/address/0xbadc0defafcf6d4239bdf0b66da4d7bd36fcf05a#code

A bot named 0xbadc0de made a windfall when traders tried to sell 1.8 million cUSDC (USDC on the Compound protocol) ($1.85 million in nominal value), but only got $500 of the asset due to low liquidity in return. However, the MEV bot made a profit of 800 ETH (~$1 million) from the sold carry trade. An hour later, a hacker exploited a bug in 0xbadc0de's badc code to withdraw all 1,101 ETH (~$1.5 million) in the contract.

On September 27, 2022, the Ethereum MEV bot '0xbad' lost over 1,100 WETH (worth about $1.4M) to an attacker exploiting a callback function designed for flash-loan protocols. The exploit used dYdX's SoloMargin contract to trick the bot into approving and draining all WETH funds. The 0xbad MEV bot contract delegated privileged callback permissions to both its owner and specific DeFi protocols, including dYdX's SoloMargin, but failed to restrict or validate the calldata enforced through these callback mechanisms. This allowed an attacker to use SoloMargin to call a crafted payload, manipulating the contract into granting token approval and enabling a follow-on transfer to drain all assets.
